newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Legal threats dog Hong Kong's future chamber.
newsitem.headline: Legal threats dog Hong Kong's future chamber.

text.p: Hong Kong's future lawmakers, fearful of possible legal challenges, failed on Saturday to agree on a formula to enact laws for the British colony before it reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.

The 60-member provisional legislature convened in the city of Shenzhen across the border in China to decide on a format for passing bills to dilute existing Hong Kong laws that protect civil liberties and rights.
But the prospect of potential legal challenges to the chamber's legitimacy prevented any decision from being reached, some members of the provisional legislature said.

"Some legal circles are of the opinion that if the provisional legislature tries to go through the procedure of passing laws before July 1, it can incite legal challenges," said provisional legislator Selina Chow.
Chow is also a member of Hong Kong's current elected legislature.

Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp says the interim chamber, crafted by China in December and poised to replace the territory's elected chamber on July 1, breaches the territory's post-handover constitution.
Democracy supporters have threatened to sue the chamber if it passes any laws, holds meetings or opens offices on Hong Kong soil before July 1.
The shadow chamber voted to take up the matter at an undecided later date.
